    Free sacred geometry downloads

    Each figure on its own, ready to use. Cut files are 12 inches wide with 0.08 inch lines. Open one in the maker to change its size, add rings or a name.

    • Seed of Life

      Seven equal circles: one in the middle and six around it, each passing through the center. It is the first stage of the Flower of Life.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Flower of Life

      Nineteen overlapping circles on a six-fold grid, inside a bounding circle. The best known sacred geometry figure, found drawn on the walls of the Temple of Osiris at Abydos in Egypt.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Flower of Life, Completed Petals

      The Flower of Life with the partial circles at its edge drawn in, so every petal against the outer ring is whole.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Fruit of Life

      Thirteen circles taken from the Flower of Life pattern. Join their centers and you get Metatron's Cube.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Metatron's Cube

      The 13 circles of the Fruit of Life with all 78 straight lines between their centers. The lines are said to hold flat drawings of the five Platonic solids.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Stars Within Stars

      A five-pointed star with smaller stars nested inside it, each turned to fit the last. Its proportions follow the golden ratio.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Mystic Rose

      Points around a circle, each joined to every other point by a straight line. The chords weave rings of stars and curves toward the center.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Golden Spirals

      Spirals that grow by the golden ratio each quarter turn, crossing in opposite directions like the spirals of seeds in a sunflower head.

      SVGCut SVGCut DXFLine DXFPDFEdit

    • Times Table Circle

      Points around a circle joined by a multiplication rule. Hundreds of straight lines trace curved, cardioid-like petals.

    How to make a sacred geometry mandala

    1. Pick a figure. In Shapes, choose a figure from the Sacred geometry group and press Add. It sits at the center and fits inside your rings.
    2. Choose a variation. Tap the layer to switch between versions, like 19, 37 or 61 circles for the Flower of Life, and to change its size or turn it.
    3. Ring it. Add petals, arches or dots around it. Use six-fold symmetry, or 12, 18 or 24, so the rings line up with six-fold figures.
    4. Download. Print a PDF coloring page, save a PNG, make a sticker, or download a cut-ready SVG or DXF.

    Leave the center open for a name

    In Design, slide Open center for words and type a name, a word or a date. The figure and rings stop at the opening, and the maker tells you how wide the opening prints on a page and on a sticker, so you know the lettering will fit. Cut files keep the center open so you can add your own lettering in your cutting software.

    Make it a sticker

    The Sticker download makes a round die-cut sticker: your design on a disc, a white border, bleed beyond the cut, and a magenta CutContour line that print then cut machines and sticker printers recognize. Try the Night glow look for gold lines on a dark disc.

    Questions

    Is the sacred geometry generator free?

    Yes. Every figure and every export is free, with no signup and no watermark, and you may sell what you make with it.

    Can I cut the Flower of Life on a Cricut or laser?

    Yes. Download the cut-ready SVG for Cricut or Silhouette, or the DXF for a laser, CNC router or plasma table. Every circle is merged into one connected outline at the size and line thickness you choose.

    How do I put a name in the middle?

    Open Design, slide Open center for words, and type a name or a date. The rings stop at the opening, and the maker shows how wide the opening will print.

    Can I make a sticker?

    Yes. In Download, the Sticker option makes a round die-cut sticker with a white border, bleed and a CutContour cut line, or a 300 dpi PNG for sticker printers.

    Why does the Flower of Life need six-fold symmetry?

    Its circles sit on a six-fold grid. Set Symmetry to 6, 12, 18 or 24 and the rings you add around it line up with its petals.
